Q: How to write UT for non-virtual functions? A:

First, an example of the problem would be helpful.

Is there any another way to cover the failed cases ?

Yes: integration tests or system tests, instead of unit tests.

Second, with TDD style unit testing, the unit tests ought to be written first. The reason to write the unit tests first is because the unit tests are a forcing function guiding the implementation of the code. That's primary 90% of the value proposition of unit tests. The secondary 9% of the value proposition is how unit tests enable aggressive refactoring. The tertiary 1% of the value proposition of unit tests is as an artifact they provide a test suite to ensure basic correctness and a front line defense against basic correctness regressions.

To phrase that a different way, unit tests are primarily a developer tool — written by developers for developers. Not primarily a quality tool. The quality that unit tests ensure is quality of the code, not quality of the application. Granted, there is a correlation between the two.

J.B. Rainsberger claims that 99% of all bugs are basic correctness bugs. I think he's grossly overstating it. I think merely 95% of all bugs are basic correctness bugs.

But sometimes unit tests are not written first. TLD – test later development. The unit tests do not guide implementation. They are missing the most important part of the value proposition, which kicks the underpinnings out of their ROI. And the danger of TLD easily slipping into TND (test never development).

On top of all that, code coverage of the unit tests is key.

If you don't have code coverage, you've got bupkis.

When I was programming in C#, using Visual Studio, NUnit, and NCrunch, unit testing wasn't a chore at all — it was actually genuinely fun! I wish C++ had something like that.

Third, unit tests are not integration tests. They serve different purposes, and different domains.

For instance, on a previous project our unit test suite took about a minute to run. Half the total run time was just launching and terminating. In contrast, our full integration test suite took about 660 hours to run (in serial). In order to make that less burdensome, we had a farm of about 120 computers to run the test suite in parallel.

Finally, unit tests have a strong relationship to design-by-contract. For languages that do not provide contracts, much of what contracts provide can be expressed as unit tests. For languages that do provide contracts (like Eiffel, Ada, D, Spec#, Sing#, or Midori#), much of what unit tests provides can be expressed as contracts (often more succinctly than in unit tests).

STLab's Adobe Contract Checking for C++ is a step in the right direction for C++, but it would be much better if those kinds of contracts had been part of the core language decades ago. (The WG21 folks have been trying to navigate these waters for many years. I hope they come up with a suitable solution and consensus.) (Adobe Contract Checking still relies on unit testing for ensuring postcondition basic correctness.)

Microsoft's Code Contracts for .NET, which was back-ported from Spec# to C#, is a cautionary tale at how hard it is to retrofit contracts into a language, as a library. I consider the Code Contracts for .NET to be a failed experiment — unsuitable for larger projects. And larger projects are the ones that most need contracts.

Q: Can't deploy to GitHub Pages after next-intl: Couldn't find next-intl config file A:

The issue is most likely that GitHub Actions cannot find your next-intl request configuration, even though it works locally.

Since you don't use a src folder, make sure your structure is:

i18n/

└── request.ts

Then explicitly configure the plugin in next.config.ts:

import createNextIntlPlugin from 'next-intl/plugin';

const withNextIntl = createNextIntlPlugin('./i18n/request.ts');

const nextConfig = {

// your config

};

export default withNextIntl(nextConfig);

Also check that request.ts is actually committed to Git:

git ls-files i18n/request.ts

If nothing is returned:

git add i18n/request.ts

git commit -m "Add next-intl request config"

git push

One more important thing: Windows is case-insensitive, but GitHub Actions runs on Linux, so verify that the path is exactly:

i18n/request.ts

not I18n/request.ts or i18n/Request.ts.

I wouldn't disable SSG or add Turbopack workarounds until you've verified the config path and Git tracking.

Q: Azure Point to Site VPN connection from IOS / IPad / IPhone A:

I was not able to force native VPN in iPhone to work with Azure VPN (IKEv2, certificate authentication), but I succeed with OpenVPN type of tunnel and an external app. Generally the whole setup procedure is described in Configure point-to-site VPN clients: certificate authentication - macOS and iOS in section "OpenVPN: iOS steps"

However there are few things that needs to be done differently:

  1. Current version of OpenVPN Connect app does not work on iPhone/iPad anymore with Azure VPN and there is no possibility to install previous version. The only application does work for me was "Passepartout, VPN Clinet". This app works also with .ovpn configuration files in the same way as OpenVPN Connect.
  2. There is missing information how to get the private key from the .pfx file. This can be done on macOS with the following command: openssl pkcs12 -in P2SChildCert.pfx -nocerts -out priv-key.pem -nodes
  3. When copying client certificate and private key into .ovpn file they need to be copied WITH certificate headers

The rest of the steps can be found in Configure server settings for P2S VPN Gateway connections - certificate authentication - Azure portal.

Q: ERROR InvalidDistribution: Invalid distribution metadata: '2.5' is not a valid metadata version A:

twine >= 7.0.0 (which in the meanwhile is released) can handle metadata version 2.5.

pip install twine -U

should do the trick.

Q: Using getElementById VBA webscraping A:

I'm not sure what URL you are point to, but I see some TR elements in the screen shot, as well as some TD elements. See the sample code below, and try to convert that to your specific use case.

Sub Dow_HistoricalData()

    Dim xmlHttp As Object
    Dim TR_col As Object, Tr As Object
    Dim TD_col As Object, Td As Object
    Dim row As Long, col As Long

    ThisSheet = ActiveSheet.Name
    Range("A2").Select
    Do Until ActiveCell.Value = ""
    Symbol = ActiveCell.Value
    Sheets(ThisSheet).Select
    Sheets.Add

    Set xmlHttp = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP.6.0")
    myURL = "https://www.fxstreet.com/economic-calendar"
    xmlHttp.Open "GET", myURL, False
    xmlHttp.setRequestHeader "Content-Type", "text/xml"
    xmlHttp.send

    Dim html As Object
    Set html = CreateObject("htmlfile")
    html.body.innerHTML = xmlHttp.responseText

    Dim tbl As Object
    Set tbl = html.getElementById("fxst-calendartable")


    row = 1
    col = 1

    Set TR_col = html.getElementsByTagName("TR")
    For Each Tr In TR_col
        Set TD_col = Tr.getElementsByTagName("TD")
        For Each Td In TD_col
            Cells(row, col) = Td.innerText
            col = col + 1
        Next
        col = 1
        row = row + 1
    Next

Sheets(ActiveSheet.Name).Name = Symbol
Sheets(ThisSheet).Select
ActiveCell.Offset(1, 0).Select

Loop

End Sub
